newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trade chases recession beaters.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trade chases recession beaters.

text.p: Nigerian shares closed higher on Friday while investors continued to head for the safe ground of companies that have proved themselves capable of maintaining profitability despite recession.
The all-share index rose to 6617.86 from 6598.04 on Thursday.
Over the week the all share index rose 0.72 percent. Since the start of the year it is 30.0 percent higher.
"Most investors want to increase their stakes in companies that have shown good results even in recession," said one dealer.
Nestle Foods added 100 kobo to close at 35.60 naira. Flour Mills rose 40 kobo to 11.20 naira and West African Portland Cement climbed 50 kobo to 35.50 naira.
The oil-marketing sector is also looking strong.
National Oil went 50 kobo higher to 35.80 naira, the same amount as Mobil which closed at 41.00 naira. Agip gained 30 kobo to 15.20 naira and Unipetrol gained 20 kobo at 42.80 naira.
"Going by the demand for these oil companies, there is no reason why they should not climb higher in the coming week," another dealer said.
Construction firms made steady gains; G. Cappa rising 30 kobo to 8.90 naira, Julius Berger 20 kobo to 7.20 naira and Costain two kobo up at 1.69 naira.
However blue chip companies which have shown themselves to be harder hit by the recession remain under pressure.
Nigerian Breweries slid 10 kobo to 11.50 naira. Afribank was down 10 kobo at 5.20 naira and Cadbury was five kobo lower at 26.45 naira.
Union Bank and Dunlop also finished five kobo down at 7.70 naira and 11.00 respectively.
